findings.topic: Adaptive forest interface and finite budget
findings.detail: Full-cube bank bijection, forward column radius, interval states on the entire cube, public two-coordinate supports, forest per completed correct leaf, projected row-degree bound, original-row side information and correct-family termination agree with the formal interface. Correctness includes zero-mass inputs. The helper remains deterministic and is charged by H(Z). R, M, K, nu, L, Q, C, N and the displayed expected-length inequality agree with AdaptiveForestLaw.budget; manuscript assumptions are no weaker than the endpoint.

Qualitative sigma=o(d), state plus combined deficit=o(P), fixed degree, positive variable b, and the explicit fixed-sigma row-budget rate match the formal declarations. Radius/bucket floors, coefficient 8, exact adaptiveRateError and eventual (8 log delta+1)/log(log_2 d) loss agree. No improved headline rate is implied by this review.

The added sentence faithfully describes fullFiber_expected_cost_of_leaf_cost. It is a supporting expected-overhead generalization; the application retains uniform N+Cs, and the old constant-overhead theorem remains a corollary.

Disjoint diagonal mismatch and core crossing entries give the factor-two improvement. The manuscript c0=eta/[4(Delta+1)^2] agrees with balanced_conditional_gap_sharp and the actual reachable-range helper endpoint. The manuscript restricts 0<eta<=1, while the sharp finite endpoints allow 0<=eta<=2; it does not claim optimality.

findings.topic: Arbitrary joint helper law and expected budgets
findings.detail: The new theorem explicitly overrides the deterministic-helper default: X and Z may have any finite joint law. Both independently chosen halves, within-row bijections, states and decoders may be branch-selected. Each branch has a common capacity s(z) for its two states, charged by E s(Z). Reachable state ranges, rather than ambient alphabet sizes, are charged. The exact deficit P-H(X|Z)=D_X+I(X;Z) is used. Deterministic and independent-public-randomness specializations are correctly stated. No linearity or independence premise has been added.

exists_fixed_native_shear chooses one rational family, degree/expansion constants, native machine and cost coefficient before every positive m. The manuscript restricts the native claim to even canonical d=2m>=2, raw row-major input/output and blank initial work tapes; it does not require blank final tapes or claim a complete-exchange/transpose decoder. The same incidence matrix is used by both expansion and output semantics. Applying the shear twice restores the raw input, so no universal normalization obstruction is claimed.

The full local-coding, motion and padding sections remain byte-identical to the pre-review source and were reread in full. Their helper conventions, restricted models, exact constants, native quantifier order, padding idle-tape/coarse-boundary caveat, and pointwise/subsequential hypotheses remain visible. The new results do not replace these guarantees or broaden them by implication.

The manuscript credits the first paper, established expander/shear/entropy ingredients and pinned Lean dependencies, treats the known prediction-game refutation as prior art, and explicitly disclaims exhaustive priority, new generic information theory, and unrestricted transposition or multiplication improvements. This pass reviewed the bibliography and attribution language; it was not a fresh exhaustive literature search.
